title: Sweet.
paragraphs:
Sweet.
But it came from something dead.
Read that again.

Because that’s not just Samson’s riddle—
that’s the secret some of us are still living.
“Out of the eater, something to eat. Out of the strong, something sweet.” (Judges 14:14)

Sounds poetic.
But it was born from compromise.

A lion killed by God-given strength…
left to rot…
then revisited.
And inside that dead thing—honey.

Samson touched what God said not to touch.
He took sweetness from a place God said stay away from (Numbers 6:6).
And then he built a riddle out of it.
Here’s the open loop you don’t want to face:

What if the “sweet” in your life…
came from something spiritually dead?

What if the blessing you’re enjoying
was never meant to be touched in the first place?
We don’t like asking that.
So we rename things.

We call it “God’s favor”…
when it’s actually tolerated compromise.

We call it “peace”…
when it’s just numbness.

We call it “open doors”…
when we forced them open.
And deep down—you know.

You felt it the first time.
That quiet check in your spirit.
That hesitation you ignored.
But the honey tasted good.
So you went back.

Again.
And again.
Let’s be honest.
Some of us are feeding on things that once had teeth.

Dead relationships that still control your heart.
Habits that God already exposed—but you manage instead of surrender.
Private sins you’ve learned to function with in public worship.

And you say,
“But there’s still good in it.”
Yes.
That’s the deception.

Sin rarely shows up ugly at first.
It drips.

Slow.
Golden.
Convincing.
James 1:14–15 says desire conceives… then gives birth to sin… and sin, when full-grown, brings forth death.
Not instantly.
Gradually.
Sweetly.
Pause.
Here’s the question you avoid when it gets quiet:

What “honey” are you defending
that God already called unclean?
And deeper—

Are you more attached to the sweetness…
than you are surrendered to the Savior?
Some scholars interpret Samson’s act as a violation of his Nazirite vow, especially touching a carcass (Judges 14:8–9). Whether he rationalized it or ignored it—the pattern is clear:

Strength on the outside.
Compromise on the inside.
And that’s the dangerous kind of life.

Because you can still be used by God…
and still be drifting from Him.
That should shake you.
Here’s the AHA moment:

Not every blessing is proof of obedience.
Sometimes it’s proof of God’s patience.
Read that again.

God is kind.
But His kindness is meant to lead you to repentance (Romans 2:4), not permission.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

You don’t have a confusion problem.
You have a surrender problem.
This is where it cuts.

You can sing on Sunday…
and still hide honey from a dead thing on Monday.

You can lift your hands…
while holding onto what God asked you to release.
And the scariest part?
It can still “work.”

Doors still open.
People still affirm you.
Life still moves.
But your heart…
Is slowly disconnecting from the voice of God.
But here’s where grace walks in.

Not soft.
Not silent.
Saving.

Because Jesus didn’t come to help you manage dead things—
He came to give you a new life.
At the cross, something greater than Samson’s riddle was revealed:
Out of death… came life.

Not borrowed sweetness—
but resurrection power.
1 Peter 2:24 says He bore our sins in His body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.

Jesus didn’t take honey from death—
He defeated death itself.
And He’s not asking you to clean yourself first.
He’s asking you to come.
Fully.
Honestly.
Now.
This is your moment.

Not later.
Not when it’s convenient.
Not when you feel ready.
Now.
Drop the honey.
Walk away from the carcass.
Bring the secret into the light.
Because 1 John 1:9 promises—if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Not shame you.
Cleanse you.
Restore you.
You are not called to live off hidden compromise.
You are called to walk in holy freedom.
You are not someone barely holding it together.
You are someone being called into truth, purity, and power through Jesus Christ.

If this exposed something in you…
good.
That’s not condemnation.
That’s conviction.
And conviction is mercy knocking.
Not hype. Formation.
Stay rooted.
You’ll need it again when temptation whispers.
And if someone came to your mind while reading this—send it to them. Quietly.
And the next message might be the one you didn’t know you needed.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
